title: Multiple Manufacturer Part Numbers
body: 100n/16V 402 components (C1 and subsequent) have different "Manufacturer Part number" markings. I suggest setting "CC0402_100NF_16V_10%_X7R" as the primary "Manufacturer Part Number" and "CC0402_100NF_16V_10%_X5R" as the "Manufacturer Part Number 1"

title: adding EEMs
body:
Since most Sinara devices out there right now do not have DIOT, a stand alone STM32/ECP5-based controller that also supports EEM would be a lot nicer for the transition period. 
Humpback is very limited in [EEM count](https://github.com/sinara-hw/Humpback/issues/16) and [FPGA size](https://github.com/sinara-hw/Humpback/issues/15) and needs the bulky Nucleo board. 

I know this is a big ask layout-wise, but would it be possible to somehow squeeze in the EEMs or potentially just do an EEM variant?

body: Lack of ESD protection may damage the IC17 input. The DIO1..4 lines on connectors J1, J2, J4 and J5 are protected.

title: THT points for GND
body:
Solid THT holes come in handy for connect the oscilloscope probe. I suggest adding one between the J7 connector and the IC2 chip, the second one maybe near the U7B , so as not to spoil the already arranged differential lines. Place near SLOT2.LVDS_7_N net maybe?
I propose 1mm hole with round pad to solder regular pin from tht reader.

title: Potential latchup when using stm programmer
body: After programming STM through CPU JTAG header and leaving it connected, each power cycle increases power consumption by ~5 mA per cycle (the effect stacks). Disconnecting the programmer resets the effect.

I2C PWR pullup
body:
It should probably be on a P3V3_MP bus, together with LM75, separated by e.g. voltage translator from STM. 

If you wanted to change configuration of power supply via I2C through J3, then you're limited by P3V3 pullup of this bus.

title: LVDS routing
body:
Some LVDS lanes are routed to banks that do not support LVDS at all 
Moreover some of them are routed to banks supplied from 3.3V (bank 0,1,2)
Some banks need resistors to emulate LVDS outputs (0,1,2)
Lanes 8-15 of each slot must be routed to MLVDS transceivers:
